findings.summary: Candidate 60a4613 (coding attempt 3) fixes every feature-r1 finding, verified in code. The bridge reader now gets (tx, parentScope, descriptor). Activation uses the owning livePending check. The displayed entry is retained on healthy reads. The held-response test drives read() through View request without calling index, and the harness gets a fresh recovery cookie. Queue commands use the correct parent and founder shapes, with the original AcceptRequest replayed. Direct deletes of bridge rows are refused while household cascade still works. The journal domain, key, corruption and wipe controls, the race, rollback-stage, quarantine and legacy controls, and the pending_readiness display are all added. The required repeat run passes 308/0/3, and the build, card adapter, retained probes, the new private probe and six native cases are bound to the candidate blobs. I am withholding PASS for two reasons. First, the queue's existing `late` rule now reports a request that became ready before its deadline as Overdue / 'Original deadline breached' once the original due time passes, and a later PrepareLateUpdate makes that breach permanent. That is a false deadline/accounting statement and it is untested. Second, the first full run on this exact source failed with an unexplained recovery_quarantined in the review release plus a React timeout. Those failures are preserved but have not been diagnosed. Full 05-A/B/G and 08-A/B stay OPEN and 07-A/B stay DONE. All three coding attempts are now spent, so any correction needs Rasna's authority.

findings.title: Ready-on-time bridge requests become 'Overdue'/'breached' after due time
findings.problem: `late=current.breach_observed||!terminal(storage_state)&&now()>original_due_at`. Bridge-ready requests deliberately stay in queue storage 'accepted', which is non-terminal, so once the original +24h due time passes, late becomes true even when ready_at was before the deadline. family-space.mjs:49 uses `overdue:queueDetail.late` for these requests. The parent card then shows 'Ready; notification not attempted · Overdue' and 'The original deadline has passed…' (LoopFamilyHome.tsx:141). The request detail shows 'Original deadline breached' (LoopFamilyHome.tsx:74), and the founder 'overdue' filter lists the request (request-queue.mjs:185). PrepareLateUpdate is still allowed after readiness, and it persists `breach_observed=!!st.detail.late` (line 163), which makes the false breach permanent in history. This contradicts the slice's truthful readiness/deadline accounting (08-B partial), where original receipt/deadline semantics stay intact and readiness is distinct from delivery. No test advances the clock past due after an on-time readiness. The native pending-hidden and original-recovery observations advanced the clock by only about 1 s.
findings.fix_check: Compute lateness from the immutable bridge ready_at: ready before or at due means not late; ready after due, or not ready and now past due, means late. PrepareLateUpdate must not record a breach for an on-time ready request. Add a test: on-time readiness, advance the clock more than 24 h, then the family card, queue detail and founder overdue filter all show no breach, and a late update keeps breach_observed false. Add a paired control where readiness happens after due and is shown as breached.

findings.title: Unexplained first-run quarantine/timeout on exact source is unresolved
findings.problem: candidate3-first-full.checks.log on 60a4613 records two failures. (1) The HTTP test failed inside readyBridgeSource, at review.command(ReleaseTestSnapshot), with code recovery_quarantined (review-service.mjs:534, private-bridge-fixture.mjs:42). This is an integrity classification raised by the accepted producer path in this slice's fixture, before any bridge write. (2) The React test timed out at line 45 waiting for the held open to be reached. The `until` budget there is about 200×15 ms (roughly 3 s plus act overhead), while family.open runs full household bridge and review history verification and the bridge tests take 15–60 s each. The isolated rerun and a second full run passed, but neither failure has a root cause. A spurious recovery_quarantined directly undermines the slice's 'refusal/healthy, not quarantine' contract. The required evidence therefore shows the checks pass, not that they pass reliably.
findings.fix_check: Either attribute the review quarantine with captured diagnostics (which check raised it, and which journal/DB identity differed) and fix it, or record it as a carried limitation with owner acknowledgement if it lies in unchanged accepted code. Make the React waits load-tolerant (deadline-based rather than a fixed iteration count). Provide at least three consecutive full npm test runs on the final source with zero failures.

findings.title: REPORT contains authoring notes, not post-execution evidence
findings.problem: The spec lists REPORT.md as 'actual implementation evidence after execution', but the file is the drafter's pre-execution note (correctly 'NOT RUN BY ME'). It does not record the candidate commit, the controller check results (including the preserved first-run failures), the native receipt binding or the carried limits. Spec allows Root to supply this in a separate documentation-only commit.
findings.fix_check: A Root documentation-only commit after the runtime commit records the exact candidate commit, all check outcomes including the first-run failures, the native case receipt and blob binding, and the carried limits: single-host recovery, raw play Start not bridge-aware (future 08-A), full-log verification cost and Windows caveats.

findings.title: Any bridged request makes the home depend on household-wide history
findings.problem: inspectRequest calls history() for the whole household, verifying every bridge command, and it runs once per bridged request on every home read. Corruption in one child's bridge history therefore returns 503 for a sibling's home whenever that sibling also has a bridged request. Each read also costs O(requests × household history) plus journal reads. This is conservative and acceptable for TEST, but it is undisclosed.
findings.fix_check: Document the household-scoped quarantine and the per-read verification cost in docs/loop/PRIVATE_BRIDGE_READINESS.md, or cache one verified history per transaction.

findings.problem: Rechecked, all r1 findings fixed: the blocker (family-space.mjs:41 passes bridgeScope(s) plus the exact descriptor); livePending (review-service.mjs:505-507); entry retention (LoopFamilyHome.tsx:93 no longer clears, and the line-99 filter decides); the direct-read held-response test (asserts indexCalls unchanged, View request → onObserved → read); the harness (advance plus a fresh-token assertion); queue shapes and original-key replay; the delete guard (016:119-133); journal controls; source, race, rollback, quarantine, profile and legacy-counter tests; pending_readiness UI. Verified unchanged and conformant: once-only primary sequence (makeReady 123-145: prelock order, real kernel.apply with the exact transition, booked→completed CAS, sealed fact, append outside transaction and serializer, ACK after reverification); branded DB adapter; ownership detected without the adapter; no Start or commit wiring (playCalls 0). Read fresh to EOF this round: private-bridge.mjs 1-162, private-bridge-journal.mjs 1-40, family-space.mjs 1-60, request-queue.mjs 1-200, LoopFamilyHome.tsx 1-150, review-service.mjs 1-60 and 359-536 (60-359 retained from my unchanged r1 read), migration 016 80-138 (1-79 unchanged from the r1 diff), both test files and the fixture in full (the main test file from the complete current diff), the docs and REPORT diff, the first-run failure log, and the review fixture hook names.
